utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, sir. Would you please stand and read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Ms. Residovic has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stojanovski. Mr. Stojanovski, we have already met, but I'd like to introduce myself officially. My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux we represent the Defence team for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Can you give us your full name, first and last name for the record, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Petre Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, before I move on to my questions, I'd like to ask you to hear what I have to say. Although we don't speak the same language, I do think that you can understand what I'm saying, and I myself understand what you're saying. However, my questions and your answers have to be interpreted for the Trial Chamber and everybody else in the courtroom to be able to follow the proceedings, my questions and your testimony. And for that reason, once you've heard my question, please pause to give the interpreters a chance to interpret my question and then go ahead with your answer. Have you understood?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, can you tell us when and where you were born?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: On the 23rd of March, 1963, in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what education do you have?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Sixth degree, that is faculty of security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When and where did you graduate from the faculty of security?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In 1984, in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you begin working in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia at any time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That same year, I started working at the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before testifying here, Mr. Stojanovski, have you ever given statements to the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We had contacts, I believe it was in 2004, when I was summoned by them to give a statement. However, due to several reasons, that statement remained unfinished and unsigned by me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you state the reasons why you failed to sign the statement although you talked to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Although the interview went through an interpreter, I thought there were misunderstandings with regards to the format in which the statement were to be taken. I believe that what I am saying needs to be -- needed to be entered, while the investigators thought that they were to rephrase it, to state there what they understood from what I was saying. Further on, there were misunderstandings related to certain facts, and I can't really remember that, after which, they threatened me in the sense that they could indict me for certain issues and their conduct went outside of the boundaries of propriety, and this is why I decided to leave the room where the interview was conducted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, is it true and correct that the Defence put it to you that the Prosecutor, in a way, considered you to be part of the joint criminal enterprise linked to the events that you have decided to testify about?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct that you had indicated this to me, although I still can't understand or find any explanation for that attitude.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why did you decide to come in and testify?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that the testimony is a citizen's obligation and duty, on the one hand, and as a member of the Ministry of Interior, I should have faith in the justice and be prepared to contribute towards ascertaining the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Stojanovski, let's go back to your professional experience. In order to speed up this part of your testimony, I'm going to ask you whether you did certain things, worked at certain jobs, and if you feel that anything is different to what I set out, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to use leading questions so that we don't dwell on these matters for too long.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that upon graduation in 1984, you started working straight away in the Ministry of the Interior, the MOI, and at the time you were a trainee, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From 1984, from the end of that year, December, when you completed your training session, you were a junior inspector for defence; and from 1984, you worked in the operative department -- or the administrative department in Skopje; and from 1986, you were junior inspector in the independent inspectorate for special purposes. Now was that the beginning your professional career as I have set out and in the years that I have quoted?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you can say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In January 1993, you became a senior inspector for clandestine weapons marketing, and in 1985, you became the main inspector for the clandestine drug trade, right, are those the facts?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but in the period between 1986 and 1993 I was promoted and I moved up the promotion scale, so I had more senior titles.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at one point were you given a managerial post in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Not until 1993, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that from 1996 until 1998 you were appointed to the duty of chief of the administration for trafficking in the crime police, and from 1998 to the year 2000, you were the head of the department for weapons trafficking, unlawful weapons trafficking?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What duty were you appointed to in May 2000, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In May 2000, I was appointed assistant to the head of the SVR, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you occupy that post?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Until the end of 2003 -- 2002, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do after that? And what assignments are you engaged on today?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In 2002, I was briefly head of the administration for illegal trafficking of drugs within the crime police, and then I was appointed assistant to the under-secretary of the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And today?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: And today I'm senior inspector in illegal trafficking with arms, within the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now tell me, in addition to your regular education and having graduated from the faculty of security, have you had any additional training or additional education, equipping you to conduct your professional duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In the period after 1995, I attended several courses and seminars related to the work in the administration for illegal trafficking with drugs and also I attended several courses related to management.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where those courses and seminars which you attended from 1995 to 2002 or to the present day were held? In Macedonia or somewhere else outside Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There were courses in Paris, courses in Germany, Bulgaria. Also some courses at the faculty of security in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also tell us, Mr. Stojanovski, who the organisers of those courses were, or seminars, which you attended within the frameworks of your professional training?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, the French Institute for Higher Education was the organiser of the course in Paris. One of the institutes of the federal police was the organiser of the one in Germany. In Bulgaria, the course was organised by the US Drugs Department, and the one I mentioned was organised by the faculty of security in Skopje. And there were several seminars organised or implemented in cooperation with certain bodies of the European Union and the Council of Europe as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in view of your education and training and professional experience, tell me please whether you know the organisations and competency of the Ministry of Interior, what the organisation set-up in MOI is?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, can you say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us how that is regulated, the powers and authority that the Ministry of Interior has. How is that regulated?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The competencies of the Ministry of the Interior are primarily regulated through the Law on Internal affairs and the Law on Organisation of the State Administration. Of course, there were other laws that also give us, as members of the Ministry of the Interior, certain tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I'm going to use some documents, I'd like to ask the usher's assistance to provide the Trial Chamber, the witness, and my colleagues with a set of documents that I'm going to use in the next part of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, would you please take a look at a document after tab 2 in your binder. It is P86, Exhibit P86. And I'm going to ask you to take a look at -- let me ask you if you've found the document first?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Law on Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: P86, yes. But we seem to have a different document on our screens. Now we have the right one. You said straight away that was the Law on Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, so I assume you're well acquainted with this law, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The law --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at Article 1, please. And since you know the law, you can perhaps answer my question straight away and tell me what Article 1 represents, what does it regulate?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This Article essentially defines the competences of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who it is who puts into practice all the points stipulated in Article 1 of the law?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, these tasks are carried out by two bodies within the Ministry of the Interior. One of them is the public security bureau and the other one is the directorate for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, can you tell me in what way these organs within the ministry perform their duties, work as organs of the Ministry of Interior, within their competence and authority?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, these are independent bodies that have their internal organisational structure that is governed by certain rule books in the ministry and where the competences of those organisational units are defined and their working tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about your own professional work and except for a short period of time when you started working and worked in the area of defence preparations, I noticed that all the rest of the time you worked in a specific department of the Ministry of the Interior. So can you tell the Court where you actually worked within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. With the exception of that period that you mentioned, I spent my entire career - and I still am there - in the department or within the crime police in the services that work in the area of crime repression.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this Law on Internal Affairs which you have before you, does it regulate the basic competences and tasks of the crime police, which is the department you worked in and which you work for today and carry out your professional duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This law contains provisions governing the work and setting forth the competences of the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now to take a look at Article 12 together with me, which is on N008-984 of the Macedonian and on page N000-8965 of the English version. What I want to ask you is this first: Do you recognise the Article, and, if so, tell me what that Article regulates?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is the Article 12 regulating the scope of work of the crime police and enumerating the competences of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me what the basic competences are.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Prevention of crime, detection and apprehension of perpetrators --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you speak more slowly. The interpreters have asked us to slow down.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the Law on Internal Affairs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There seems to be an interruption in the English interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we may now be on the air. I think perhaps we should have the last answer again, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovski, would you repeat what you just said and give your answer again to my question. And the question was, what the competences are according to the law under Article 12 and which you, as the crime police had.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 12, the crime police performs the following duties: It works on preventing criminal offences, detecting and apprehending the perpetrators of criminal offences, police forensic activities, supervision of residence and movement of aliens, inspection and supervision in protection from fires and explosions, as well as other activities from Article 1 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you, Mr. Stojanovski, to tell me this. Is that the only law which defines the work of the crime police, or are there other rules and regulations about that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There are also other regulations. One of the main ones, although all laws are important, is the Law on Criminal Procedure. However, there are also laws that provide for the obligations for the crime police, for example, the Law on Arms, the Law on The Border, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And except for those law, for the law, your powers and the way in which you execute those powers, are they regulated by other regulations that are not actually laws?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The work is also regulated by many by-laws, rules of procedure, and internal acts of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, when you spoke about your powers and competence, I understood it that in 2001, you were the assistant head of the sector for internal affairs for Skopje and that you were the assistant for the crime police, in the crime police. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, before this Court, Mr. Stojanovski, we heard testimony from a number of witnesses about the work and organisation of the Ministry of the Interior, and so I'm not going to ask you about what we have heard about from other witnesses, but in view of the position you occupied in the security sector, Skopje, I'd like to ask you a few questions. And, in order to do that, would you first take a look at the following document, which you will find after tab 4, and this is Exhibit 1D107. Can you tell me first whether you recognise this document, and is it one of the rules or book of rules which is important for the work of the crime police?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This document is in fact the Rules governing the organisation and work of the Ministry of the Interior and one of the basic book of rules which we implement in our everyday work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you some questions about the competence and authority as set out in this book of rules, tell me whether you know who it is in the ministry who enacts books of rules like this and other rules and regulations. Who does that, which authority?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The competency for drafting and enacting books of rules lies with the minister of the interior. He is bound by the Law on the Interior to enact acts such as these.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, please, whether you know whether there are other rules and regulations which authorise the minister in passing general acts and bringing in general acts of this kind?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I believe the Law on Organisation of the Civil Service generally lay out the competencies and authorisations of ministers in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the beginning you said that the work of the organs of the interior were carried out within two basic bodies which independently carried out their duties which are regulated by law. Tell me, now, please, which body does the crime police belong to?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The crime police is part of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How does that bureau for public security -- how is it structured? Is it divided up in any way, in order to perform these duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: As I previously said, the bureau for public security is a body of the Ministry of the Interior, which independently carries out its duties and tasks. For performing these duties, its internal organisation comprises of two, I would call, basic parts: One, the unit of police, what is often called police in uniforms; and the other unit of crime police. And, of course, there are also other organisational units which are no less important, but it is these two units that work for these units. They all work as support for the work carried out by these two units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This public security bureau and the Ministry of Interior in general, are they organised in a centralised manner? Are there branch offices in which affairs that the Ministry of Interior does are carried out?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: For the purpose of carrying out the internal affairs, the territorial principle is applied. There are organisational units which are charged with carrying out the internal matters on a given territory. These are sectors for internal affairs, which in --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting you, but my learned friend across the way would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, no, I can easily wait until the witness finishes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then go ahead, witness, and finish what you were saying. You were describing the regional organisation.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: As I said, they are organisational units based on a territorial principle for the purpose of carrying out internal affairs. These are sector of internal affairs, which contain units for internal affairs, as operative units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just as a point of clarification, Your Honour, I'm sorry for the interruption. At least in the English transcript the responses to my learned colleague's questions are put in the present tense, for example regarding the structure and organisation of the Ministry of Interior. And I'm just wondering as a point of clarification is the witness speaking about structure and organisation at present time, or as structures and organisation existed back in 2001. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, what you are speaking about now, is that related to your knowledge about the structure that existed in 2001, when you were the assistant to the head of the SVR Skopje in 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is how I understood you, because the questions were related to my position at that time, which I had at the Ministry of the Interior at the time, and this is the organisational structure which I listed. Currently the Ministry of Interior has a different organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. I believe that it is now clear. You explained that regional structure within which there are sectors for internal affairs and departments for internal affairs --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Units for internal affairs, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- tell me, please, considering the post you held in 2001, were you at that moment superior to the units for internal affairs, OVRs, on the territory of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: My tasks and my job duties were to perform the tasks appointed to the head of SVR Skopje. Most of my duties were to alleviate the management, which meant that I did not have a managerial position vis-a-vis the other units. What I did was to facilitate more efficient and quality execution of the functions of the chief of SVR Skopje. My relationship was towards the head, the chief of SVR Skopje, and so were my tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And speaking practically about what you were -- tasks that you were carrying out, what was your relation and communication to the OVRs on the territory of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know if I was clear enough. Let me put it this way: The head of SVR Skopje directly is the direct superior of the heads of the OVRs. Is this enough as a clarification?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is completely clear. And considering that you, as you stated, were the assistant to the head of the SVR Skopje for the crime police, how can we understand what you are saying? I assisted the head of the SVR Skopje in performing his duties. Were you, in a way, still communicate and what were you gathering, if I may put it that way, from the branch offices of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: One of the tasks which the head of SVR Skopje has is to coordinate activities of the OVRs. I was charged to follow the situation in the OVRs from the point of view of the crime police and to suggest, if necessary, to the head of the SVR certain solutions which could help him carry out his function of coordination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a managerial position at that time, towards anyone?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In SVR Skopje, there were organisational units which were established with the aim of securing support for the work of the OVRs. These organisational units needed to have personnel with special skills, especially trained personnel, and equipped with special material and technical means.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When explaining your role, you stated a while ago that one of the main functions of the sector was the function of coordination. Tell me, what are the functions that the sector for internal affairs has as a whole, within the Ministry of the Interior, and especially in relation to the units, the OVRs, that are within it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I will mention the two most important things. One we already mentioned, the coordination of activities between the OVRs; and, secondly, securing support for the OVRs. If, in their everyday work, they face the need of specialised personnel or are faced with the need of police forensic activities, we were obliged to secure this for them. This was done with respect of principles of effective and efficient performance of duty, and due to economic reasons, it would be irrational for each OVR to be equipped with equipment which is expensive and which will not be sufficiently utilized.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give an example?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: For example, the unit for crime police is equipped for carrying out on-site investigations. If, on the territory of an OVR - in Skopje at that time there were five such OVRs - needed to carry out an on-site investigation, they requested it from us and we secured it for them. This is the assistance we secured for them. In the case of yet another example. In -- if in the course of its work, they came to an understanding that certain criminal offences overlapped with other OVRs, then the sector -- or, rather, the unit for organised crime and coordination came in to coordinate the activities between the involved OVRs. Also, another example, cases where -- where adequately trained personnel was required, for example, in the area of organised crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I understood now what were the main roles of the sector for internal affairs. And tell me now, in 2001, what were the competences and the responsibilities, as well as the organisation, in the units for internal affairs, OVRs?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The unit of internal affairs has police stations as part of its composition, also sector for criminalistic affairs, and a unit for analytics. These were all charged to act on the territory covered by the OVR. I mean these departments. The departments act on the territory of the OVR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we should clarify this a bit further. Tell me, in the area of crime police, who was the -- carrying out the operations that the Law on Internal Affairs prescribed? So who had the duty to detect perpetrators of crimes, et cetera, et cetera, on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know whether we understand each other on this. On a given territory, there is an OVR which is in charge of carrying out the tasks listed in the Law on the Interior, on that given territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you stated there are police stations there, also the crime police department and the analytics. In those OVRs, in those departments, there are -- the officers are employed by the Ministry of the Interior. What are the competences of those officers?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Their status is that of authorised official persons as all other police workers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what are the ways in which they perform their duties? What is the basis for the performance of their duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understand you well. However, they work on a given territory and they're independent in carrying out their work. They're independent and bound to carry out the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who is responsible for the work of all those police officers in the police station, in the unit for internal affairs, whether it is the analytics, the crime police or whatever else?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe I mentioned that this is the head of the OVR. He is the head of the unit and he is directly in charge of the departments and the police stations which I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if by chance those members of the MOI were not performing their duties in accordance with the law, as you stated, who would then be the person who would need to raise the issue of their responsibility?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is their direct superior. In this case, this would be the head of the OVR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So from what you stated, my understanding is that the superior over the OVR is the head of the sector for internal affairs, Skopje, or the assistant to the minister for internal affairs for Skopje, while the rest of you who are employed with the SVR Skopje don't have superior duties over the OVR. Is that your evidence thus far, or have I misconstrued it maybe?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I think we understand each other well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And considering this situation, were you able to issue orders to the heads of the OVRs on the territory of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. In accordance with my position, I could not issue orders to the OVRs. However, on the other hand, they had the obligation to inform us of things that happened which were on their territory and under their competency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me, in 2001 who was the head of the sector for security for Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This was Mr. Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you for SVR Skopje. Maybe ...

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There was a change. Up until September, it was Mr. Efremov. From September onwards, Mr. Kocovski. My apology.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Krstevski. What duties did he have in 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: He was one of the heads of the OVRs in Skopje. We had five such OVRs, and he was the head of OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if somebody were to testify to the contrary, quite the opposite to what you said in this Court, and if they were to say that you yourself were the individual who was superior to the heads of the departments of the internal affairs, in this view, what would you say to that kind of testimony and those assertions?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There are two explanations. Either someone is lying or that someone has not worked in SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's go back to what the crime police does, the duties of the crime police. You said a moment ago that the OVR, the departments of the internal affairs, are engaged in the affairs of the crime police. Now, this department, does it have a separate title, a separate name, or is it just called "crime police"?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a department for operative works.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if view of this title or name, what are its tasks linked to carrying out the work of the crime police? What level of work is this, of this operations department?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: These are employees of the crime police who, according to their name, are operative and directly carry out tasks. This is the basic thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you said that one of the important laws that determine the work of the crime police was the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you to look at a document which you'll find after tab 3. It is Exhibit P88. Do you recognise this law, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Law on Criminal Procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, underneath the title "Law on Criminal Procedure," you will find the revised version of the text from the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia. Now my understanding of this is that in the text we find certain provisions which were in -- adopted or enacted after 2001. And that's why I want to ask you whether the amendments in this Official Gazette, 44/02, whether they were amendments which had to do with the tasks of the organs of the interior in criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. These changes did not change the position of the crime police. This happened somewhat later; I believe it was in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we can use this text of the law with regards to the tasks of the organs of the interior in the scope of criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you something about your remitt and your competencies tell me to what extent do the organs of the interior, what links do they have to the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, and what is your understanding, briefly, of the position of the office of the public prosecutor in relation to the pre-trial procedure?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If I can express myself freely, usually sometimes they say that they're the head and we are the hands. This means that the public prosecutor and his obligations allow him to ask certain tasks of us and to give guidelines for our work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said that you worked on the uncovering of crimes, now, does the public prosecutor have any competencies within that regard? But before you go ahead and answer, let me ask you this: Do you know, in general terms, that in keeping with the rules and regulations of the Republic of Macedonia, that criminal procedure actually starts? When does it start, at what point?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: With the start of the investigation. According to our legislation there are two phases: A pre-trial phase and criminal procedure. Our competencies as a Ministry of the Interior and members of the crime police relate to the pre-trial procedure and, with exception, in the criminal procedure when we act upon the request of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely what I wanted us to clarify. And as you said, that the -- well, you said that the prosecutor was the head and that you were the hands. So that was a colloquial description. But in this pre-criminal procedure stage, what is the role of the public prosecutor, in relation to the tasks that you yourself have in conformity with the law?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: He is responsible for detecting and prosecuting of perpetrator of criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And with relation to the stage before criminal proceedings go ahead, does he have any special powers?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Surely the law gives him such authorisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask to you look at this code on criminal procedure and to look at Article 42 of that code, which is on page N001-9029 of the Macedonian; and the English version is to be found on page N001-9187, or page 11 in the English. This is a provision, or Article, which, sets out the duties of the public prosecutor. I'd just like to draw your attention to point (2) of (1) where it says that: "For crimes which are prosecuted ex officio the public prosecutor is duty-bound to take necessary measures in relation to uncovering the crimes and apprehending the criminals and to direct the preliminary procedure, preliminary procedure." Now tell me, please, what -- in addition to the fact that he uncovers crimes himself and attempts to uncover the perpetrators, what, in your opinion, does it mean when it says that in the preliminary procedure he directs, in fact, the preliminary procedure. What does that mean? What must he do? What are his duties in that respect? And what is your position vis-a-vis the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that I stated that the public prosecutor holds a superior position over the crime police and that they have the duty, the public prosecutor has the duty, to take measures to uncover crimes and their perpetrators. Also the public prosecutor is the only one who can ask that an investigation -- request that an investigation is carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now to clarify this still further by using an example, when an organ of the interior - for instance, you, the crime police - inform the prosecutor about an event which you had reason to believe was a crime, what is the procedure put in place and what is your relationship? What must you do after that has been established?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I think I mentioned already we have a subordinate position. Our task is to follow, to execute the request and to follow the directions given to us by the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you worked to uncover crimes yourself and the perpetrators thereof, how do -- does the crime police, as part of the interior, how do you inform the prosecutor about the information you obtain?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There are several situations here. If, in the course of our work, we arrive at an information that a crime has been committed, and if we have sufficient relevant facts to substantiate the notion that such crime had been committed and the identity of the perpetrator is unknown to us, then we file a criminal report against an unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the perpetrator is known to you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If we have a suspect for the crime, then usually, in the practice, we file a criminal report that might be in writing, might be oral. What is important is -- however, the law provides other ways in which the public prosecutor can be informed of that issue. This also applies to the cases when the perpetrator is unknown.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if I understood you correctly a moment ago, you said that if the perpetrator or perpetrators were unknown and the police has enough facts to go by, which indicate that a crime had indeed been committed, then they file a criminal report against perpetrators unknown. Now, tell me, please, Mr. Stojanovski, if -- or, rather, what happens if the organs of the interior and the crime police just have rumours to go by or information that hasn't been checked out with the facts that a crime had been committed? What are your duties in cases of that kind? For example, if you read about something in the papers, if the papers say that such-and-such a thing happened.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we have the duty to carry out checking of the facts and to provide at least minimum of relevant facts and information that could corroborate the notion that a crime had indeed been committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you don't find those relevant facts to back up your suspicions, what do you do then?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Then usually the case is archived or, as we say, it is left at stand by. So if any new information arrived, they could be connected, correlated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what you're saying is this: If you have insufficient proof and evidence for reasonable doubt that a crime had been committed, if you don't have the grounds for that, is it still your duty to inform the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If we have not succeeded in establishing or if we do not have relevant information that a crime had been committed, then we don't have the obligation to inform the public prosecutor. Then the case remains in the archives of our service.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: However - I apologise - there is another position. As well as we can react, the same obligation belongs to the public prosecutor. Maybe he chooses to involve us, but he does not have that duty. If he chooses to involve us, then we have the duty to follow his orders and to take measures and activities that agree with the directions given by the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if the public prosecutor has heard about the same case, he might have read it in the papers, for instance, and he considers that the event might constitute a crime, then he selects the organs of the interior and tells them what to do, issues instructions to them. And once that is done, what do you then do with the material? Do you archive it or do you have other duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. In that case, we have the duty to inform the public prosecutor of the measures that we had taken. And depending on the outcome, we either file a report against a perpetrator unknown, if we had established that a crime had indeed been committed, or, we inform the prosecutor by an Official Note that we had not established that a crime had been committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you, Mr. Stojanovski, to take a look at Article 144, paragraph 2, of the Code on Criminal Procedure, which is to be found on N001-92058 of the Macedonian; and in English it is on page 34. Yes, that's right, page 34. As you explained the different duties and the possibilities open to the police and the public prosecutor, I'm going to read out para 2 of this Article, and I'd like you to tell me whether what it says here is confirmation of what you have testified about in this Court, or, are there certain matters that you would like to clarify further. It says: "If the public prosecutor cannot evaluate from the report whether the contents of the report are probable, or if the data of the report do not provide a sufficient basis to decide whether opening of an investigation is to be requested, or if the public prosecutor had only heard allegations that a crime had been committed, especially if the perpetrator is unknown, the public prosecutor, if he is unable to do it himself or through other bodies, he will request the Ministry of Interior to collect necessary information and take other measures to uncover the crime and the perpetrator." And then in brackets the Articles 142 and 143 are quoted. And then the public prosecutor may always request the Ministry of the Interior to inform the prosecutor of the measures undertaken. Is this the provision that you mentioned as the prosecutor being able, alone or in other way, to verify information but that when you are requested to provide information, then you have the duty to inform the prosecutor about the measures undertaken?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I tried to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now within the frameworks of that provision, we see that the code refers to Articles 142 and 143, do you know what Articles 142 and 143 regulate? Whose rights and duties are regulated in those two Articles?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: It indicates the duties of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, if I have understood you correctly, when you answered a moment ago and told us who carries all this out. I think you told us that.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that I mentioned that in the units for internal affairs, OVRs, there are subunits for operations and for crime police, and they have the duty to perform those tasks. Of course this does not preclude the uniformed police from taking certain actions, but usually it is the crime police that takes and performs those duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in carrying out the duties set out in these Articles of the Code governing criminal procedure, in practice, what is the most usual way to go about things? How does the crime police and other organs of the interior arrive at information that a crime has actually been committed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The usual way is when a complainant makes a report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who files a criminal report providing you with the information, usually?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, in cases of thefts, usually the owner is the complainant. In cases of homicides; that is the victim. So the injured parties are the ones who are the complainants.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the importance of this link between the internal affairs organs with the injured party, in uncovering both the crime and the perpetrator thereof?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The importance is major. Primarily, since, as I mentioned before, we already have -- when the injured party makes a report, we already have some relevant facts that indicate that a crime had been committed, while the other aspect is that the victim can provide very useful data. The injured party can provide us very useful data that will guide us towards uncovering the perpetrator of that crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And vice versa, in a reverse situation if the injured party or plaintiff does not want, for any reason, or rejects cooperation with the police, does not wish to cooperate, what effect does that have on the possibility of you carrying out your tasks properly? How does that affect your work?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: We have had such cases in the practice. I can say that it is exceptionally difficult to process them. It is practically impossible without the cooperation of the injured party.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now you've answered some of my questions in great detail and very precisely. And a moment ago you were saying that some of your powers or the authority you have and work was regulated by rules and regulations. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Your Honours, this is a good time to take a break. I don't want to go on for too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Residovic. We will have the break now and resume -- is half an hour enough for a break, do you think, for your comfort, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, would you look at the document that is found after tab 8. It is Exhibit P96, and the page in Macedonian is 042-4644 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to comment just two Articles -- to hear comments on two Articles, but I would like to tell you that it is a document we discussed yesterday. We discussed it and the Prosecutor discussed it, too. There's a draft translation, and -- no, I have been informed by my colleague that what I was about to say concerned another document, so not this document. I made a mistake because I know there was a problem with this document too but not the type of problem that I was going raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Anyway, would the witness look at Article 103 and 104 of these rules. Tell me, first of all, is this an important set of rules, important for the work of the crime police?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, and it is being implemented in our everyday work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 103 is on page ERN --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Residovic repeat the numbers, please. It was too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] R042-4638, and the English version is on the following page. I have to find the page number. I don't seem to have it. It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So would you look at Article 103 first, please. And with respect to that Article, I'd like to say that part of the text is being revised. So I'm going to read the Articles out and the interpreters can interpret to avoid any problems. Mr. Stojanovski, in Article 103, it says the following: "In the case of grounds of suspicion that a criminal act has been committed which is prosecuted ex officio, the authorised official persons undertake the necessary measures to find the perpetrator of the criminal offence so as to avoid the accomplice of hiding or fleeting, to discover and secure evidence of the criminal offence and the artifacts that can serve as evidence in the criminal procedure and to collect information that can be of benefit for successful performance of the criminal procedure. Now, in connection with that, Mr. Stojanovski, I'd like to ask you this: In the first paragraph, it says that the measures are undertaken if there are grounds to believe that a crime had taken place. Now, what I'd like to ask you is this: Is it the principle task of the police, especially the crime police, to establish whether there are grounds to suspect that a crime had been committed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this was mentioned in your previous statement, that, first, there has to be relevant information and to corroborate a fact that a criminal offence has been committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, I've shown you these two Articles so that you can confirm whether these Articles reflect what you testified to in answering my questions. Article 104 states the following: "In order to establish the existence of grounds of suspicion that a criminal offence has been committed, it is necessary to know certain relevant facts and data on the basis of which it is possible seriously to presume that a crime offence has been committed." Now, that provision - and this is my question - does that provision in fact confirm what you yourself were saying when you said that you, first of all, have to have grounds to believe that a crime had been committed, and that once you had those grounds, serious grounds, you would take steps?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I hope that I was able to explain this when -- in my previous answer, but this is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the operative organs of the OVR were organs which, independently, took steps to check and establish whether an incident constituted a crime or not, and if it did constitute a crime, to proceed further and uncover the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The interior affairs organs, when are they duty-bound to take those measures? Is there a deadline, a period within which they are supposed to take those steps?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Measures are under taken until the public prosecutor is informed, or until the investigating judge becomes involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, if there are grounds to suspect that a traffic incident, for example, was a crime in -- as stipulated by the code governing traffic, what is the -- what steps should the police take and when do their duties cease? This is to say, when is the case taken over by other organs? When do other organs take on the responsibility to initiate further proceedings?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The procedure should be as follows: The crime police, members of the Ministry of Interior, are bound to secure the site, to undertake measures to preserve evidence and while this is done the investigating judge and the public prosecutor is notified. At this moment once they are notified of the incident, they can decide whether the on-site investigation will be given over to the MOI, or whether they will come to the site and will directly lead with the investigation. In the second alternative, if they do come to the site once we have notified them, the obligations of the members of the MOI - that is to say, the crime police - cease. This means that they are obliged to act following the orders of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, can the police influence the investigating judge's decision, how he is going to rule?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In no way and in no case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when the court has been informed by the police, is the police duty-bound to file another criminal report to the prosecutor, or, rather, to inform the judge once again about the event?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In accordance with my experience, if the investigating judge comes to the site, he is duty-bound to prepare minutes, that is to say, to document the case, and this means an end of our duties for further communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already told me that the operative organs, the operatives of the interior affairs department, take up all measures that the police does to uncover the perpetrators in their particular area. And specifically, if we take the town of Skopje, for example, how many such units or departments of internal affairs do you have, and where did their responsibilities end with respect to uncovering crimes and uncovering the perpetrators of crimes?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: As I said earlier when I was explaining the organisational structure of SVR Skopje, I mentioned that there are five OVRs. They are the only ones that carry out the internal matters in the area for which that OVR has been established. After having taken all the measures, especially until the notification of the investigating judge and the public prosecutor, I believe I already said earlier, their duties end.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you've explained that quite clearly. So the duties of the police, to take further steps, after it has informed the prosecutor or the judge, ceases there. Now, tell me, please, is the police duty-bound later on, if the prosecutor or the judge requests it to do something, whether it must follow up on that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The obligation ends. However, we are duty-bound to act upon the requests or the orders issued by the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, it is clear to me that your duties have ceased. Now, what I would like to know is this: Can the police gather some other evidence, for instance, and can it refuse to take over information which, after it has informed the prosecutor or judge, new information has arrived?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The judge is the one who decides to whom a certain task for a case will be assigned to. However, in the case which you have just now mentioned, the police can inform the investigating judge or the public prosecutor about information it receives afterwards. Therefore, the police can do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just to be sure that I understood you correctly, what you've just said, did you say in fact that it is the duty of the police to take steps until it informs the prosecutor or the judge and when -- once it has done so, it can undertake other measures but it is no longer obliged to, it no longer has the obligation to do so?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is why I used the word "can."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, let's see what happens in the period of time before the prosecutor or judge has been informed about a specific event. You said that the measures are taken by the operatives, the operative organs, or, rather, the internal affairs department or unit. Now, the internal affairs unit, in a given area, can it -- before it informs the prosecutor or the judge, can it be relieved of its duties of investigation?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: These are legal obligations, and I believe it cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Stojanovski --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly. Would you -- could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the situation before the internal affairs organ has informed the public prosecutor or the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Apology.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I understand you correctly you said up until that time the internal affairs organs are duty-bound and had the responsibility of uncovering a crime and the perpetrators thereof. Right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let me take it a step further. During that period of time when you had that obligation, when the internal affairs has that obligation and responsibility within a commune or the OVR, for instance, that organ, can it be relieved of those duties? Can it be relieved of its duty to react when a crime has taken place or to investigate a crime or relieved of identifying a perpetrator or any other measures which generally it is duty-bound to undertake during that stage, until the case is taken over by the prosecutor and the judge --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and wait for interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... contrary to the legal obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So can he be relieved of that duty?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask the witness to repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, would you repeat the answer, please. Can they be relieved of that duty before they inform the prosecutor or judge?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: It cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Stojanovski, if before this Court somebody were to testify and say that he did not take steps, the adequate steps because, at that point in time, there were persons superior to him in the place he was at, what would your comments to that be? What would you say to that? Is it possible that somebody who is duty-bound by law to react, can he be relieved of that duty because there was a superior person there?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is no such case in practice. It does not relieve that person of his duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said you haven't had such cases in practice. But by law, can they be relieved of their duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the presence of a superior officer in a place where a crime has been committed does not relieve the organs of the interior from conducting their duties who are duty-bound to act?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In essence, it doesn't matter who is present there. They are duty-bound to carry out the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a unit within the department of the interior is not capable of taking steps and measures itself, what happens then, in practice and pursuant to the rules and regulations of the MOI of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In that case, they can request assistance from the SVR, from the sector of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And based on your experience, can any operative measures be taken by the ministry itself, at the level of the Republic, in uncovering crimes and the perpetrators thereof?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: According to the Law on Internal Affairs they have no operative functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How about the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In particular, the minister. His competencies are defined in the Law on Internal Affairs. According to those competencies, there is no mention of an obligation pertaining to operative tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you this, Mr. Stojanovski, if I were to put it this way, now the fact that this legal obligation does not exist, that is to say that the minister should take some operative steps to uncover crimes, does that mean that the minister should not be interested in the state of affairs where crime is concerned, or do you mean to say something else?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: One cannot go to extremes. The minister has political responsibility for the situation for the area he is responsible for, including crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if the minister were to form some commissions, for example, for them to look into a given situation linked to crimes committed, based on your experience, would those commissions replace or could they replace the legal obligations of -- that the organs have to uncover crimes?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: When we are talking about crime, for example, if the minister shows a certain interest about a specific event, then he has the right to establish commissions and working groups that will, in a way, work and elaborate on the case and inform him of it. In my experience, such commissions and working groups have been established on numerous occasions, and in view of my position at that time, they came to ask about certain events. They asked that interviews be conducted or materials be sent to them. This is a customary practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And since you were the head of the crime police for the city of Skopje, if I understood you well, then such group or a committee did not relieve you of the responsibility to perform your duties as stipulated in the law?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, not at all. These are completely different matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if, for instance, someone from the OVR failed to perform their duties properly, in what way would you, from the SVR or from the MOI, need to react?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If the direct superior does not carry out his tasks, or does not act according to his competencies, he is subject to disciplinary measures. Depending on the case, he may be even liable for criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And since, for instance -- if, for instance, the direct superiors from the OVR or the head of SVR failed to do that, within which body organ of the internal affairs would the question of enforcement of the law be raised? For instance, with regards to the situation within the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If you mean about the quality of work, then this should be primarily evaluated by the bureau for public security. If we're talking about a sector for internal affairs, then the bureau for public security is the body that evaluates the work of the sector and assesses the quality of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since you mentioned the director of the public security bureau, do you know who appoints the director of the bureau for public security?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The director is an appointed official. This means the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know, whom is he accountable to?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Usually he is accountable towards the ones who has appointed them. This means the government and the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And while we're speaking about the director as an official, tell me, we followed the line, so if the director fails to react about the situation of the enforcement of the law performance in a sector or somewhere, who was then the only one who could dismiss the director of the bureau for public security?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The procedure says that the minister is the one who should submit a proposal to the government about the dismissal of the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, if I understood this answer properly, the minister does not have competences to sanction the director. The minister can only propose the government to take certain measures. Is that what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's a bit late for me now, but that seemed to be a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is true, Mr. Saxon, and it is true it is a bit late.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe if you look at this question alone, it is absolutely a leading question as you say. But before that, the witness said the same thing. I just repeated it through a leading question, and I apologise for that, but it was not unfounded, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have been cautioned that Mr. Saxon is anxious. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Stojanovski, in addition to what you said about your understanding of the duties and responsibilities of the minister, tell me, have you ever been close to the minister in your practice, or have you ever received any orders from a minister, any minister, because probably there were several ministers throughout your career?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: For my 25/6 years of professional experience, many ministers have passed through the ministry, and I have not encountered a situation like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone would assert before this Court that the minister directly called a person from the OVR and ordered them to take certain actions, what would be your comment to such assertion?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If I can express myself freely -- may I express myself freely? This would be boasting. Only a person who would like to present himself in a loftier position than he is would say this. I'm not saying that it's not possible, but this does not happen in practice. Especially I can speak of myself, this has never happened to me, although I have been on senior position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a minister had called a certain person, you said everything is possible, so the minister could, for instance, call the phone number of a policeman, of a patrol police officer. Tell me, so if something like that happened, actually, that some minister calls the head of the OVR, does this relieve that person from the responsibilities that are vested to that person under the law?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is no such law. There is no such Book of Rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you to look at the document after tab 5. That is Exhibit 1D106, and it provides a brief definition of the bureau for public security. So I will read it. It says: "The administration is led by a director/head, who, pursuant to a proposal by the minister is appointed and removed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia, for a term of office of four years. "The director is independent in the performance of the works of the administration, and is accountable for his work to the minister and the government of the Republic of Macedonia. "Upon a proposal of the director of the administration, the minister adopts -- passes acts for the organisation and work, enforces systemization of the jobs within the administration to which the government of the Republic of Macedonia provides consent." My question is, Mr. Stojanovski, whether this brief description of the position and of the duties of the public security bureau correspond to your personal knowledge as of 2001, with regards to the position of the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Of course. I think even in my previous statements I made comments to that extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look again after tab 4. That is Exhibit 1D107. And let's turn to page 1D4390; and the English page is 1D4414. Before that, I kindly ask to you look at the page before that one. And in the lower right corner you will see that this rule back was passed on the 26th of January, 2001, by the then minister of interior, Dosta Dimovska. And in Article 28 of this rule book, it is indicated that the diagram of the internal organisation of the ministry with its headquarters and the territorial organisational forms are the integral parts of this rule book. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you now to look together at this diagram. That is 1D4390, or 1D4414. Towards the middle of this diagram, we see the public security bureau. Tell me, please, whether this diagram reflects your evidence before this Court, that parts of the public security bureau exist and that they perform -- that they enforce the law independently?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And here we see also the crime police department, where you worked also in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. On these matters, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, in addition to this central diagram of the public security bureau, you see also some bodies that are linked to the minister, but -- but they are related to the public security bureau also with broken lines. Considering that they are linked to the minister, I would like to ask you now the following. On the top of this table you see the special tasks unit Tiger. Do you know -- or, rather, did you know in 2001 about the existence of the special units task force Tiger?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they existed in the course of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Having this diagram in mind, was the minister able to issue orders to this special tasks unit, Tiger?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: My personal opinion, the scheme is not really adequate. The minister could only approve the use of this special unit. No more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, according to this diagram, he was able to order the use of that unit. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This -- this is what I said, to approve the use of that special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would such order mean that the minister assumes the command of this unit?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. This is altogether something different. The Minister has the right to approve at someone's request the use of this special unit. However, the command is something entirely different. This is not something which falls as a right of the minister. I was not a member of the special unit, but from my own experience, I know how this was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then who is the commander, when the use, the deployment of this unit is ordered? Who is then the commander of this unit?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The commander commands this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are there situations when this commander has the duty to execute other orders?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: As I said, the scheme may not be most adequate. The special task units, in their structure, are within the framework of the bureau for public security. In the police unit, there is a sector for special purposes, special unit -- special task unit, and this is the link with the unit for special tasks. The special tasks unit carries out its regular work duties and organisational duties through the sector for special task units. The minister can approve the deployment of this unit. However, the unit itself is, if I can say, within the hierarchy of the special unit sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand this really, so I might reframe the question. In this diagram, bearing the date January 2001, we see that the special unit Tiger is linked to the minister. Was that the situation that existed permanently or do you have any knowledge about some changes with regards to the position of the special unit Tiger or --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: An unnatural position. The way it is depicted on this scheme, this is unnatural. It's inadequate for the special units Tiger. If memory serves me right, at one period of time, possibly this was the period, the special tasks unit was subordinate to the minister. But immediately it was noted that this was a mistake, so it was returned within the sector for special units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you -- very well. Thank you. I believe that we elaborated on this sufficiently and I still appreciate the fact that I will ask you more about the crime police, but thank you very much for this clarification that you gave us just now. I will ask you now to move to a different topic. You were the assistant to the head of the SVR Skopje, so maybe I should better ask you more specific questions about the events in Skopje. In 2001, could you briefly tell us what were the circumstances in which the police acted within the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is possible to explain in brief. In this period, the security situation was extremely complex, and if I were to look at the situation more broadly, two aspects have to be taken into account: The resources which we had available; and the situation which we were facing. In that period of time, I think it's well known that the Republic of Macedonia was - how to say? - in an armed conflict.
